ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p42/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p42/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p42/r5.claim: The indefinite word “register” magnifies it: this is no ordinary record but one preserving every detail, as 18:49 illustrates.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p42/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p42/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p42/r6.claim: Moses says God's register preserves minute detail, not omitting anything small or great.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p42/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p42/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p42/r7.claim: God neither errs nor forgets; nothing escapes His knowledge, becomes distorted, or is erased.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p42/r7.anchor: The Almighty neither makes a mistake nor forgets

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p42/r8.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p42/r8.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p42/r8.claim: Moses answers with dignity that his Lord accurately knows everything, including the histories of nations vanished from earth.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p42/r8.anchor: His Lord has accurate information of everything

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p42/r9.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p42/r9.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p42/r9.claim: The record serves accountability and later reward or punishment; Moses leaves this implication unstated because insinuation can communicate more than explicit speech.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p42/r9.anchor: to subject them to accountability and to subsequent reward and punishment

ASAD-NOTES:20:51#n33/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:20:51#n33/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:20:51#n33/r1.claim: God alone decrees earlier generations' afterlife destiny because He knows their motives and errors and can assess their spiritual merits and demerits.
ASAD-NOTES:20:51#n33/r1.anchor: He alone knows their motives and understands the cause of their errors

ASAD-NOTES:20:51#n34/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:20:51#n34/r1.speaker: Razi
ASAD-NOTES:20:51#n34/r1.claim: Razi takes the dialogue to end temporarily at this point and verses 53-55 as direct discourse to humanity.
ASAD-NOTES:20:51#n34/r1.anchor: According to Razi, the dialogue between Moses and Pharaoh ends here for the time being, with verses 53-55 representing a direct Qur'anic discourse addressed to man in general

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:25/r12.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:25/r12.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:25/r12.claim: Pharaoh's question about past generations may imply that powerful people escape consequences; Moses answered that they remain within God's knowledge and records, and God neither errs nor forgets.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:25/r12.anchor: Ardından Firavun gelip geçen nesillerin durumunu sorarak muhtemelen, dünyada güç sahiplerinin yaptıklarının yanına kâr kaldığına işaret etmiş ve Mûsâ’dan buna açıklık getirmesini istemişti. Hz. Mûsâ onların da rabbinin bilgisi dışında olmadığını ve her şeyin Allah katında kayıtlı bulunduğunu ifade etmiş

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:25/r13.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:25/r13.speaker: Râzî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:25/r13.claim: Razi's favored reading is that Pharaoh changed the subject to distract Moses from a compelling answer that might persuade the audience; Moses recognized this and gave a general reply.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:25/r13.anchor: Râzî’nin tercihe şayan gördüğü yoruma göre ise, Firavun’un gelip geçen nesillere dair soru sorması konuyu değiştirme ve Hz. Mûsâ’yı hikâye türü açıklamalara çekip meşgul etme amacı taşıyordu

BURSEVI:v5p303#4/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p303#4/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p303#4/r1.claim: Knowledge of earlier generations' circumstances belongs to the unseen known only to God; knowledge of them is not part of the Messenger's office beyond what God reveals.
BURSEVI:v5p303#4/r1.anchor: إن علم أحوال تلك القرون من الغيوب التي لا يعلمها إلا الله ولا ملابسة للعلم بأحوالهم بمنصب الرسالة

BURSEVI:v5p303#4/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p303#4/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p303#4/r2.claim: Their detailed circumstances are recorded in the Preserved Tablet.
BURSEVI:v5p303#4/r2.anchor: أي : مثبت في اللوح المحفوظ بتفاصيله

BURSEVI:v5p303#4/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p303#4/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p303#4/r3.claim: He defines error as missing an object in its place and forgetting as losing it from awareness; both are impossible for the One who knows essentially.
BURSEVI:v5p303#4/r3.anchor: الضلال أن تخطىء الشيء في مكانه فلم تهتد إليه والنسيان : أن تغفل عنه بحيث لا يخطر ببالك

BURSEVI:v5p303#4/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p303#4/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p303#4/r4.claim: God neither errs in knowing any information nor forgets it over time; the Tablet's record is not needed for His knowledge but displays events to angels as evidence of its perfection.
BURSEVI:v5p303#4/r4.anchor: والمعنى لا يخطىء ابتداء بل يعلم كل المعلومات ولا يغفل عنه بقاء بل هو ثابت أبدا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p341/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p341/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p341/r2.claim: The apparent referent of their knowledge is the earlier generations: their record is with God in the Preserved Tablet, beyond error or forgetfulness.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p341/r2.anchor: والظاهر عود الضمير في علمها إلى القرون الأولى أي مكتوب عند ربي في اللوح المحفوظ لا يجوز عليه أن يخطىء شيئا أو ينساه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p341/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p341/r3.speaker: الفراء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p341/r3.claim: Al-Farra explains ḍalla as missing or failing to find something in its place; the form with hamza is used when a lost animal escapes.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p341/r3.anchor: يقال: ضللت الشيء إذا أخطأته في مكانه، وضللته لغتان فلم يهتد إليه كقولك: ضللت الطريق والمنزل ولا يقال أضللته إلا إذا ضاع منك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p341/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p341/r4.speaker: الزجاج
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p341/r4.claim: Al-Zajjaj says ḍallaltuhu means placing something somewhere and not knowing where it is; aḍlaltuhu is when it goes missing.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p341/r4.anchor: وقال الزجاج: ضللته أضله إذا جعلته في مكان ولم تدر أين هو، وأضللته

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p341/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p341/r5.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p341/r5.claim: An alternative says the pronoun refers to the Day of Resurrection, since Pharaoh asked about the resurrection of nations.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p341/r5.anchor: وقيل: الضمير في علمها عائد على القيامة لأنه سأله عن بعث الأمم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p341/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p341/r6.speaker: السدي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p341/r6.claim: Al-Suddi glosses lā yaḍillu as God not becoming heedless.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p341/r6.anchor: وقال السدي لا يضل لا يغفل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p341/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p341/r7.speaker: ابن عيسى
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p341/r7.claim: Ibn ʿIsa says lā yaḍillu means nothing escapes God's knowledge, citing an Arabic expression about a dwelling being lost.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p341/r7.anchor: وقال ابن عيسى لا يضل لا يذهب عليه تقول العرب ضل منزله بغير ألف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p341/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p341/r8.speaker: مقاتل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p341/r8.claim: Muqatil supplies an implied object: God neither loses the book nor forgets what it contains.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p341/r8.anchor: وقيل: التقدير لا يضل ربي الكتاب ولا ينسى ما فيه قاله مقاتل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p341/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p341/r9.speaker: القفال
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p341/r9.claim: Al-Qaffal says God does not err in knowing things and never loses that knowledge; the second clause signals its permanence.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p341/r9.anchor: وقال القفال لا يضل عن معرفة الأشياء فيحيط بكل المعلومات ولا ينسى إشارة إلى بقاء ذلك العلم أبد الآباد على حاله لا يتغير

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p341/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p341/r10.speaker: الحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p341/r10.claim: Al-Hasan says God does not mistake the time of resurrection or forget it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p341/r10.anchor: وقال الحسن: لا يخطىء وقت البعث ولا ينساه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p341/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p341/r11.speaker: مجاهد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p341/r11.claim: Mujahid regards the two clauses as equivalent, showing that nothing alters God's knowledge.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p341/r11.anchor: وقال مجاهد: معنى الجملتين واحد وهو إشارة إلى أنه لا يعرض في علمه ما يغيره

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p341/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p341/r12.speaker: ابن جرير
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p341/r12.claim: Ibn Jarir says God does not err in planning by judging wrong to be right, and does not forget what He knows.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p341/r12.anchor: وقال ابن جرير: لا يخطىء في التدبير فيعتقد في غير الصواب صوابا وإذا عرفه لا ينساه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p341/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p341/r13.speaker: أبو عبد الله الرازي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p341/r13.claim: Al-Razi rejects literal containment of divine knowledge in a book: the record is an analogy for knowledge's enduring retention; alternatively, the recorded decrees let angels infer God's omniscience.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p341/r13.anchor: علم الله صفة قائمة به ولا تكون حاصلة في الكتاب لأن ذلك لا يعقل، فالمعنى أن بقاء تلك المعلومات في علمه كبقاء المكتوبات في الكتاب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p342/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p342/r1.speaker: الحسن، قتادة، الجحدري، حماد بن سلمة، ابن محيصن، وعيسى الثقفي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p342/r1.claim: Their reading with ḍamma on yāʾ means God does not let the book go astray and does not forget what He recorded in it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p342/r1.anchor: وقرأ الحسن وقتادة والجحدري وحماد بن سلمة وابن محيصن وعيسى الثقفي لا يضل بضم الياء أي لا يضل الله ذلك الكتاب فيضيع ولا ينسى ما أثبته فيه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p342/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p342/r2.speaker: السلمي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p342/r2.claim: Al-Sulami reads both clauses passively, presenting error and forgetfulness as denied of God.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p342/r2.anchor: وقرأ السلمي لا يضل ربي ولا ينسى مبنيتين للمفعول

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p342/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p342/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p342/r3.claim: The apparent syntax makes both clauses independent reports that God is free of these qualities; another analysis makes them modifiers of book with an omitted pronoun.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p342/r3.anchor: والظاهر أن الجملتين استئناف وإخبار عنه تعالى بانتفاء هاتين الصفتين عنه. وقيل: هما في موضع وصف لقوله في كتاب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p342/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p342/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p342/r4.claim: The apparent subject of forgetfulness is God, though it may refer to the book, with forgetting used metaphorically for leaving nothing unrecorded.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p342/r4.anchor: والظاهر أن الضمير في ولا ينسى عائد على الله. وقيل: يحتمل أن يعود على كتاب أي لا يدع شيئا فالنسيان استعارة كما قال إلا أحصاها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p342/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p342/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p342/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas says God will leave neither those who disbelieve nor those who affirm Him without recompense.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p342/r5.anchor: وعن ابن عباس لا يترك من كفر به حتى ينتقم منه ولا يترك من وحده حتى يجازيه

ALUSI-FULL:v16p203#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p203#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p203#2/r1.claim: Moses answers that the generations’ detailed histories are unseen matters known only to God; he is a servant who knows only what revelation gives him for his mission.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p203#2/r1.anchor: أي أن ذلك من الغيوب التى لا يعلمها إلا الله تعالى وإنما أنا عبد لا أعلم منها إلا ما علمنيه من الأمور المتعلقة بالرسالة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p203#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p203#2/r2.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v16p203#2/r2.claim: Another view is that Pharaoh asked to test whether Moses was a prophet or merely a storyteller familiar with old nations.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p203#2/r2.anchor: سأله عن ذلك ليختبر أنه نبى أو هو من جملة القصاص الذين دارسوا قصص الأمم

ALUSI-FULL:v16p203#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p203#2/r3.speaker: النقاش
ALUSI-FULL:v16p203#2/r3.claim: Al-Naqqash says Pharaoh asked after hearing the believer from Pharaoh’s family warn his people of the day of the confederates; Moses returned the knowledge to God because the Torah had not yet been revealed.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p203#2/r3.anchor: وقال النقاش : أن اللعين لما سمع وعظ مؤمن آل فرعون

ALUSI-FULL:v16p203#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p203#2/r4.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v16p203#2/r4.claim: One view links the question to “peace on whoever follows guidance”: Pharaoh asks about the dead generations’ happiness or misery, and Moses says God knows the detail.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p203#2/r4.anchor: وقال بعضهم : أن السؤال مبنى على قوله عليه السلام ( والسلام على من اتبع الهدى )

ALUSI-FULL:v16p203#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p203#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p203#2/r5.claim: Al-Alusi says the preceding general statement already answers that interpretation: whoever follows guidance is safe, while whoever turns away is punished.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p203#2/r5.anchor: فاندفع ما قيل : أنه لو كان المؤول عنه ما ذكر من السعادة والشقاوة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p203#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p203#2/r6.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v16p203#2/r6.claim: Another proposal links the question to the revelation claim: why did earlier generations deny it and then suffer punishment?
ALUSI-FULL:v16p203#2/r6.anchor: إذا كان الأمر كذلك فما بال القرون الأولى كذبوا ثم ما عذبوا

ALUSI-FULL:v16p203#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p203#2/r7.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v16p203#2/r7.claim: A further view takes the question to concern resurrection and the pronoun in “their knowledge” to refer to the Day of Judgment; al-Alusi dismisses these proposals and especially the pronoun’s reference to resurrection.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p203#2/r7.anchor: هو متعلق به والسؤال عن البعث والضمير فى ( علمها ) للقيامة وكلا القولين كما ترى

ALUSI-FULL:v16p204/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p204/r1.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v16p204/r1.claim: One interpretation makes Pharaoh challenge how God could encompass the details of numerous, ancient peoples; Moses replies that divine knowledge includes them all.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p204/r1.anchor: اعتراضا على ما تضمنه من علمه تعالى بتفاصيل الأشياء وجزئياتها المستتبع

ALUSI-FULL:v16p204/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p204/r2.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v16p204/r2.claim: The generations are singled out because Pharaoh knew some of them and could test Moses’ truth, or because he wanted to trap Moses quickly before a broad answer prolonged matters.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p204/r2.anchor: وتخصيص القرون الأولى على هذا بالذكر مع أولوية التعميم قيل لعلم فرعون ببعضها وبذلك يتمكن من معرفة صدق موسى

ALUSI-FULL:v16p204/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p204/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p204/r3.claim: Al-Alusi calls this interpretation remote and rejects the objection that naming earlier peoples weakens it, since naming all things would make the trap clearer and stronger.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p204/r3.anchor: فانه لو اخذها بجملتها كان أظهر وأقوى في تمشى ما اراد

ALUSI-FULL:v16p204/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p204/r4.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v16p204/r4.claim: Another challenge asks why earlier peoples failed to infer the Creator from such a clear proof; a related view asks why they did not infer from God’s guidance, with both answers referring to divine decree.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p204/r4.anchor: ما بال القرون الأولى نسوه سبحانه ولم يؤمنوا به تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v16p204/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p204/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p204/r5.claim: “Their knowledge is with my Lord, in a book” is parsed with “with my Lord” as the first predicate and “in a book” as the second; Abu al-Baqa lists alternatives, but a verbal noun cannot govern beyond its predicate.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p204/r5.anchor: الظاهر أنه خبر ثان لعلمها والخبر الأول عند ربى وجوز أن يكونا خبرا واحدا مثل هذا حلو حامض

ALUSI-FULL:v16p204#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p204#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p204#2/r1.claim: Al-Alusi prefers “with my Lord” as the first predicate and “in a book” as the second; the book may be the Preserved Tablet, with its actual inscriptions standing for the recorded knowledge.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p204#2/r1.anchor: وانت تعلم أن أول الأوجه هو الأوجه وكأنه عنى عليه السلام بالكتاب اللوح المحفوظ أي علمها مثبت في اللوح المحفوظ بتفاصيله

ALUSI-FULL:v16p204#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p204#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p204#2/r2.claim: Alternatively, “book” can mean an ordinary register, a simile for how firmly the knowledge is established in God’s knowledge; al-Alusi considers this perhaps preferable, as the next clause suggests.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p204#2/r2.anchor: وجوز أن يكون المراد بالكتاب الدفتر كما هو المعروف فى اللغة ويكون ذلك تمثيلا لتمكنه وتقرره فى علمه عز وجل

ALUSI-FULL:v16p204#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p204#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p204#2/r3.claim: On either reading, “He neither errs nor forgets” prevents the thought that God records matters because he fears forgetting; the Tablet’s record instead serves divine purposes.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p204#2/r3.anchor: والظاهر أن فيه على الوجهين دفع توهم الاحتياج لأن الأثبات في الكتاب إنما يفعله من يفعله لخوف النسيان

ALUSI-FULL:v16p204#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p204#2/r4.speaker: القفال وبعض المحققين
ALUSI-FULL:v16p204#2/r4.claim: Al-Qaffal and some investigators take “does not err” as never omitting anything from divine knowledge and “does not forget” as never losing what is already known; al-Alusi approves this reading.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p204#2/r4.anchor: وتفسير الجملتين بما ذكر مما ذهب اليه القفال ووافقه بعض المحققين ولا يخفى حسنه

ALUSI-FULL:v16p204#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p204#2/r5.speaker: مجاهد
ALUSI-FULL:v16p204#2/r5.claim: Mujahid is reported to treat the two verbs as synonymous; al-Alusi says this is not sound.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p204#2/r5.anchor: وأخرج ابن المنذر وجماعة عن مجاهد أنهما بمعنى واحد وليس بذاك

ALUSI-FULL:v16p204#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p204#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p204#2/r6.claim: Grammarians either take the verbs as intransitive or as transitive with an omitted object: nothing, or the affairs of the earlier generations, is lost or forgotten.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p204#2/r6.anchor: والفعلان قيل : منزلان منزلة اللازم وقيل : هما باقيان على تعديهما

ALUSI-FULL:v16p204#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p204#2/r7.speaker: الحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v16p204#2/r7.claim: Al-Hasan says God does not err about or forget the time of resurrection; al-Alusi notes that this assumes Pharaoh asked about resurrection.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p204#2/r7.anchor: وعن الحسن لا يضل وقت البعث ولا ينساه وكأنه جعل السؤال عن البعث

ALUSI-FULL:v16p204#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p204#2/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v16p204#2/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets the promise as God not leaving a disbeliever without retribution or a monotheist without reward, apparently reading the question as one about their ultimate state.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p204#2/r8.anchor: وعن ابن عباس أن المعنى لا يترك من كفر به حتى ينتقم منه ولا يترك من وحده حتى يحازيه

ALUSI-FULL:v16p204#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p204#2/r9.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v16p204#2/r9.claim: Some make the clause an adjective of “book,” with an omitted return pronoun; another parses God as the object, so nothing can make the book lost to him and it omits nothing, like the cited verse.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p204#2/r9.anchor: وزعم بعضهم أن الجملة فى موضع الصفة لكتاب والعائد اليه محذوف أي لا يضله ربى ولا ينساه

ALUSI-FULL:v16p205/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p205/r1.speaker: الحسن وقتادة والجحدري وحماد بن سلمة وابن محيصن وعيسى الثقفي
ALUSI-FULL:v16p205/r1.claim: They read “does not lead astray” with a prefixed damma on the yāʾ, from the form meaning to cause something to be lost.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p205/r1.anchor: بضم الياء من اضل واضللت الشئ وضللته قيل بمعنى

ALUSI-FULL:v16p205/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p205/r2.speaker: ابن السكيت
ALUSI-FULL:v16p205/r2.claim: Al-Sikkit distinguishes losing one’s camel from losing one’s way to a mosque or provisions, and generalizes the latter to stationary things whose location cannot be found.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p205/r2.anchor: يقال : اضللت بعيرى إذا ذهب منك وضللت المسجد والزاد إذا لم تعرف موضعهما

ALUSI-FULL:v16p205/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p205/r3.speaker: أبو البقاء
ALUSI-FULL:v16p205/r3.claim: For this reading, Abu al-Baqa parses “my Lord” either as the object no one can lead away from knowledge or as the subject that does not find the book lost.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p205/r3.anchor: جعل ( ربى ) منصوبا على المفعوليه والمعنى لا يضل أحد ربى عن علمه

ALUSI-FULL:v16p205/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p205/r4.speaker: السلمي
ALUSI-FULL:v16p205/r4.claim: Al-Sulami reads both verbs in the passive, with the agent unspecified.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p205/r4.anchor: لا يضل ربى ولا ينسى ببناء الفعليت لما لم يسم فاعله

ALUSI-FULL:v16p205/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p205/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p205/r5.claim: Al-Alusi marvels that interpreters abandon the apparent meaning for such strained constructions.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p205/r5.anchor: والعجب كل العجب من العدول عن الظاهر إلى مثل هذه الأقوال

ALUSI-FULL:v16p205/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p205/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p205/r6.claim: Repeating “my Lord” instead of a pronoun gives pleasure in naming God, adds emphasis, and signals that lordship itself entails freedom from error and forgetfulness.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p205/r6.anchor: واظهار ( ربى ) فى موقع الاضمار للتلذذ بذكره تعالى ولزيادة التقرير

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p277/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p277/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p277/r2.claim: Moses replies that God has preserved their deeds and will requite them for them.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p277/r2.anchor: أي: أعمالهم محفوظة عند الله يجازي بها.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p277/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p277/r3.speaker: unnamed view
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p277/r3.claim: Another view says Moses referred the matter to God because he did not know it; the Torah was revealed after Pharaoh and his people perished.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p277/r3.anchor: وقيل: إنما رد موسى علم ذلك إلى الله لأنه لم يعلم ذلك، فإن التوراة أنزلت بعد هلاك فرعون وقومه.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p277/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p277/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p277/r4.claim: The book is the Preserved Tablet.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p277/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p277/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p277/r5.claim: One gloss says God does not err; another says nothing escapes Him or is absent from Him.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p277/r5.anchor: لا +يخطئ. وقيل: لا يضل (2) عنه شيء ولا يغيب عن شيء

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p277/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p277/r6.speaker: unnamed view
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p277/r6.claim: One gloss says God does not err about their deeds and so can requite them; another says He does not leave matters undone, but punishes disbelievers and rewards believers.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p277/r6.anchor: ما كان من أمرهم حتى يجازيهم بأعمالهم. وقيل: لا ينسى أي: لا يترك، فينتقم من الكافر ويجازي المؤمن.

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:52/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:52/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:52/r1.claim: Moses says the earlier generations' fate is unseen known only to God; he is a servant like Pharaoh and knows only what God revealed to him.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:52/r1.anchor: أي هو غيب لا يعلمه إلا هو وإنما أنا عبد مثلك لا أعلم منه إلا ما أخبرني به

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:52/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:52/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:52/r2.claim: Their knowledge being in a book may mean it is recorded in the Preserved Tablet.

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:52/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:52/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:52/r3.claim: Alternatively, this is a metaphor for God's knowledge being firmly retained, like information a scholar preserves by writing it down.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:52/r3.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون تمثيلا لتمكنه في علمه بما استحفظه العالم وقيده بالكتبة

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:52/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:52/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:52/r4.claim: To err is to miss an object's location and fail to find it; to forget is for it to leave one's mind, and neither is possible for the One who knows by essence.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:52/r4.anchor: والنسيان أن تذهب عنه بحيث لا يخطر ببالك

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:52/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:52/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:52/r5.claim: Pharaoh's question may challenge how God's power can encompass all things and assign different forms and properties, which requires knowledge of every detail and particular.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:52/r5.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون سؤاله دخلا على إحاطة قدرة الله تعالى بالأشياء كلها وتخصيصه ابعاضها بالصور والخواص المختلفة

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:52/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:52/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:52/r6.claim: The answer is that God's knowledge encompasses all earlier peoples and their parts and states, all recorded with Him; He neither errs nor forgets.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:52/r6.anchor: علمه تعالى محيط بذلك كله وأنه مثبت عنده لا يضل ولا ينسى

BIQAI-FULL:v5p22#2/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p22#2/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p22#2/r2.claim: Moses refuses an unproductive argument about the generations; the Torah had not yet been revealed, since it came after Pharaoh's destruction.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p22#2/r2.anchor: لم تكن التوراة نزلت عليه إذ ذاك , وإنما نزلت بعد هلاك فرعون

BIQAI-FULL:v5p22#2/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p22#2/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p22#2/r3.claim: The generations' knowledge is with God in a book, identified as the Preserved Tablet; God describes it through the familiar human practice of keeping records.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p22#2/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p22#2/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p22#2/r4.claim: God has assigned angels to record His servants' affairs, another familiar reason to speak of a book.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p22#2/r4.anchor: وكان تعالى قد وكل بعباده من ملائكته من يضبط ذلك

BIQAI-FULL:v5p22#2/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p22#2/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p22#2/r5.claim: God's knowledge neither misses any aspect nor forgets any report or other matter.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p22#2/r5.anchor: ولا نسي وجها يدخل منه شيء من خلل

BIQAI-FULL:v5p22#2/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p22#2/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p22#2/r6.claim: This rebukes Jews: if prophethood required an answer to every question, they would have to doubt their own prophet, who did not explain the generations to Pharaoh.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p22#2/r6.anchor: وفي ذلك إشارة إلى تبكيت اليهود بأن ثبوت النبوة

BIQAI-FULL:v5p23/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p23/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p23/r5.claim: The world's provisions meet every creature's needs across changing conditions, for their journey to God and presentation before Him; this completeness proves God does not err or forget.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p23/r5.anchor: أبدع هذا العالم شاملا لكل ما يحتاجه من فيه لما خلقهم له من السفر إليه والعرض عليه

BIQAI-FULL:v5p23/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p23/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p23/r6.claim: Unlike God, a human maker eventually discovers defects in a product and must repeatedly work to remove them.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p23/r6.anchor: لو عمل شيئا واجتهد كل الاجتهاد في تكميله

DURR-FULL:v5p582/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p582/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p582/r4.claim: “My Lord does not go astray” means that He does not err.
DURR-FULL:v5p582/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله: {لا يضل ربي} قال: لا يخطئ

DURR-FULL:v5p582/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p582/r5.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v5p582/r5.claim: He takes “does not go astray” and “does not forget” as one and the same idea.
DURR-FULL:v5p582/r5.anchor: عن مجاهد رضي الله عنه في قوله: {لا يضل ربي ولا ينسى} قال: هما شيء واحد

DURR-FULL:v5p582/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p582/r6.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v5p582/r6.claim: He reads “does not go astray” as referring to the Book and “does not forget” as referring to what it contains.
DURR-FULL:v5p582/r6.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه في قوله: {لا يضل ربي ولا ينسى} قال: {لا يضل ربي} الكتاب {ولا ينسى} ما فيه

DURR-FULL:v5p582/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p582/r7.speaker: أبو المليح
DURR-FULL:v5p582/r7.claim: He counters criticism of belief in the Book by citing that the generations’ knowledge is with God in a Book.
DURR-FULL:v5p582/r7.anchor: عن أبي المليح قال: الناس يعيبون علينا الكتاب وقال الله تعالى: {علمها عند ربي في كتاب}

DURR-FULL:v5p582/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p582/r8.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v5p582/r8.claim: When asked about the Book, Qatada says there is nothing wrong with it, since God the All-Knowing informs of it.
DURR-FULL:v5p582/r8.anchor: عن أبي هلال قال: كنا عند قتادة فذكروا الكتاب وسألوه عن ذلك فقال: وما بأس بذلك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p233#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p233#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p233#2/r1.claim: Bāl can denote an important state or condition, as in 47:2, and can also mean a thought or opinion; its choice here is a subtle rhetorical feature.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p233#2/r1.anchor: والبال : كلمة دقيقة المعنى ، تطلق على الحال المهم ، ومصدره البالة بتخفيف اللام ، قال تعالى : { كفر عنهم سيآتهم وأصلح بالهم } ( محمد : 2 ) ، أي حالهم . وفي الحديث ( كل أمر ذي بال . . . ) الخ ، وتطلق على الرأي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p233#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p233#2/r2.speaker: فرعون
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p233#2/r2.claim: Pharaoh may ask about Egypt's earlier generations to suggest that Moses calls their ancestors collectively mistaken, a distracting tactic used when one lacks a real argument; compare 10:78.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p233#2/r2.anchor: أراد فرعون أن يحاج موسى بما حصل للقرون الماضية الذين كانوا على ملة فرعون ، أي قرون أهل مصر ، أي ما حالهم ، أفتزعم أنهم اتفقوا على ضلالة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p233#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p233#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p233#2/r3.claim: Alternatively, Pharaoh changes the topic after Moses' case succeeds: either answer about punishment would provoke descendants or validate Pharaoh, and the creation discussion may also prompt inquiry about the dead's fate; the question is meant to frustrate and distract.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p233#2/r3.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون المعنى أن فرعون أراد التشغيب على موسى حين نهضت حجته بأن ينقله إلى الحديث عن حال القرون الأولى : هل هم في عذاب بمناسبة قول موسى : أن العذاب على من كذب وتولى } ( طه : 48 )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p233#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p233#2/r4.speaker: محمد
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p233#2/r4.claim: On the first interpretation, Moses avoids an unproductive discussion of the dead because his mission addresses the living, resembling the Prophet's answer when asked about polytheists' children: God knows what they would have done.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p233#2/r4.anchor: وهذا نظير قول النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لما سئل عن ذراري المشركين فقال : ( الله أعلم بما كانوا عاملين )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p233#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p233#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p233#2/r5.claim: Moses' answer that their knowledge is with his Lord in a book fits both readings: he declines fruitless inquiry about the dead, or frustrates Pharaoh's attempt to divert him from his mission.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p233#2/r5.anchor: وقول موسى في جوابه { علمها عند ربي في كتاب } صالح للاحتمالين ، فعلى الاحتمال الأول يكون موسى صرفه عن الخوض فيما لا يجدي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p234/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p234/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p234/r1.claim: Moses avoids debating matters outside his mission; he knows the earlier generations' general circumstances but not every individual detail.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p234/r1.anchor: والحاصل أن موسى تجنب التصدي للمجادلة والمناقضة في غير ما جاء لأجله لأنه لم يبعث بذلك . وفي هذا الإعراض فوائد كثيرة وهو عالم بمجمل أحوال القرون الأولى وغير عالم بتفاصيل أحوالهم وأحوال أشخاصهم .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p234/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p234/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p234/r2.claim: In علمها, the possessive construction makes the verbal noun's pronoun its object; the pronoun refers to القرون الأولى, whose collective noun may take a feminine pronoun.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p234/r2.anchor: وإضافة { علمها } من إضافة المصدر إلى مفعوله . وضمير { علمها } عائد إلى { القرونن الأولى } لأن لفظ الجمع يجوز أن يؤنث ضميره .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p234/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p234/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p234/r3.claim: In a book may metaphorically mean detailed knowledge, or imply certainty because written matters are established; al-Harith ibn Hilliza's line illustrates the latter, reinforced by God's not erring or forgetting.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p234/r3.anchor: وقوله { في كتاب } يحتمل أن يكون الكتاب مجازا في تفصيل العلم تشبيها له بالأمور المكتوبة ، وأن يكون كناية عن تحقيق العلم لأن الأشياء المكتوبة تكون محققة كقول الحارث بن حلزة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p234/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p234/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p234/r4.claim: God's not straying means not erring in knowledge, likened to missing a road; not forgetting means not failing to recall what is known.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p234/r4.anchor: والضلال : الخطأ في العلم ، شبه بخطأ الطريق . والنسيان : عدم تذكر الأمر المعلوم في ذهن العالم .

FARRA:v2p180/r4.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p180/r4.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p180/r4.claim: لا يضل ربي means that God does not forget; ربي is nominative, with an omitted pronoun as the object of يضله in the coordinated لا ينسى.
FARRA:v2p180/r4.anchor: أي لا ينساه و (ربي) في موضع رفع تضمر الهاء في يضله

FARRA:v2p180/r5.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p180/r5.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p180/r5.claim: أضللت describes something that escaped and became lost, like an animal; ضللته has two dialectal forms for misplacing a fixed object such as a house, and is not said with أضللت.
FARRA:v2p180/r5.anchor: وتقول: أضللت الشيء إذا ضاع مثل الناقة والفرس

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p47/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p47/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p47/r9.claim: The book may mean the Preserved Tablet or the record angels wrote of human circumstances.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p47/r9.anchor: وقوله في كتاب يريد في اللوح المحفوظ أو فيما كتبه الملائكة من أحوال البشر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p47/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p47/r10.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p47/r10.claim: A reading with fatḥ on the yāʾ and kasr on the ḍād begins a new sentence that exalts God above erring and forgetting; here ḍalāl means becoming lost or confused.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p47/r10.anchor: وقرأت فرقة «لا يضل» بفتح الياء وكسر الضاد واختلف في معنى هذه القراءة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p47/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p47/r11.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p47/r11.claim: Another interpretation makes the predicates describe the written record: it is never lost from God, using the Arabic idiom for something missing from its owner.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p47/r11.anchor: وقالت فرقة بل قوله لا يضل ربي ولا ينسى من صفات الكتاب أي إن الكتاب لا يغيب عن الله تعالى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p47/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p47/r12.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p47/r12.claim: A Prophetic report about the Israelite who asked to be burned after death uses the expression laʿallī aḍillu Allāh as an example of the verb meaning to be lost.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p47/r12.anchor: ومنه قول النبي صلى الله عليه حكاية عن الإسرائيلي الذي طلب أن يحرق بعد موته «لعلي أضل الله» الحديث

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p47/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p47/r13.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p47/r13.claim: The apparent referent of yansā is God, though some interpretations return it to the book, metaphorically meaning that it omits nothing, as in the record that leaves nothing uncounted.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p47/r13.anchor: وينسى أظهرها ما فيه أن يعود ضميره إلى الله تعالى ويحتمل أن يعود إلى الكتاب في بعض التأويلات يصفه بأنه لا ينسى أي لا يدع شيئا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p292/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p292/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p292/r1.claim: Moses’ answer means that God knows the deeds of the earlier generations.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p292/r1.anchor: فقال علمها عند الله أي علم أعمالها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p292/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p292/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p292/r2.claim: An alternative takes the pronoun in ‘its knowledge’ as referring to the Resurrection, since Pharaoh asked about the nations’ resurrection.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p292/r2.anchor: وقيل الهاء في علمها كناية عن القيامة لأنه سأله عن بعث الأمم فأجابه بذلك

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p292/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p292/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p292/r3.claim: The book in which this knowledge is recorded is the Preserved Tablet.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p292/r3.anchor: وقوله في كتاب أراد اللوح المحفوظ

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p292/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p292/r4.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو وعاصم الجحدري وقتادة وابن محيصن
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p292/r4.claim: These readers pronounce yāʾ with ḍamma and ḍād with kasra, meaning God does not let the matter slip away.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p292/r4.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله بن عمرو وعاصم الجحدري وقتادة وابن محيصن لا يضل بضم الياء وكسر الضاد أي لا يضيعه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p292/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p292/r5.speaker: أبو المتوكل وابن السميفع
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p292/r5.claim: Abu al-Mutawakkil and Ibn al-Sumayfaʿ read yāʾ with ḍamma and ḍād with fatḥa.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p292/r5.anchor: وقرأ أبو المتوكل وابن السميفع لا يضل بضم الياء وفتح الضاد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p292/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p292/r6.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p292/r6.claim: The verse confirms recompense for deeds: God neither errs nor forgets their affairs before repaying them; an alternative reading of the point questions whether the matter was written lest God err or forget.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p292/r6.anchor: وفي هذه الآية توكيد للجزاء على الأعمال والمعنى لا يخطئ ربي ولا ينسى ما كان من أمرهم حتى يجازيهم بأعمالهم وقيل أراد لم يجعل ذلك في كتاب لأنه يضل وينسى

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p298/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p298/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p298/r2.claim: Moses answers that their deeds were recorded by God in the Preserved Tablet and the record of deeds, and He will repay them accordingly.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p298/r2.anchor: عند الله مضبوط عليهم، وسيجزيهم بعملهم في كتاب الله، وهو اللوح المحفوظ وكتاب الأعمال

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p298/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p298/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p298/r3.claim: Nothing, large or small, escapes God and He forgets nothing; unlike creatures, His knowledge has neither lack of comprehension nor forgetting.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p298/r3.anchor: أي: لا يشذ عنه (7) شيء، ولا يفوته صغير ولا كبير، ولا ينسى شيئا.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p69/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p69/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p69/r2.claim: Moses says he knows only what the Knower of the unseen has revealed; the generations' histories are recorded with God in the Preserved Tablet.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p69/r2.anchor: وما أنا إلا عبد مثلك لا أعلم منه إلا ما أخبرني به علام الغيوب ، وعلم أحوال القرون مكتوب عند الله في اللوح المحفوظ

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p69/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p69/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p69/r3.anchor: لا يجوز على الله أن يخطيء شيئا أو ينساه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p69/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p69/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p69/r4.claim: The verb “miss” can mean failing to find something in its place, like losing a road or home.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p69/r4.anchor: يقال : ضللت الشيء إذا أخطأته في مكانه فلم تهتد له ، كقولك : ضللت الطريق والمنزل

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p69/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p69/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p69/r5.claim: A reading with the causative form means that God does not lose or neglect anything.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p69/r5.anchor: وقرىء ( يضل ) من أضله إذا ضيعه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p69/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p69/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p69/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains that God does not leave an unbeliever without punishment or a monotheist without recompense.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p69/r6.anchor: وعن ابن عباس : لا يترك من كفر به حتى ينتقم منه ، ولا يترك من وحده حتى يجازيه

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p405#2/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p405#2/r12.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p405#2/r12.claim: Moses returned knowledge of the earlier generations to God.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p405#2/r12.anchor: { قال علمها عند ربي } فرد موسى علم ذلك إلى ربه .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p405#2/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p405#2/r13.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p405#2/r13.claim: The phrase may mean God did not put their knowledge in a book because He might stray or forget it.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p405#2/r13.anchor: أي لم يجعل علم ذلك في كتاب لأنه يضل أو ينسى .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p405#2/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p405#2/r14.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p405#2/r14.claim: Alternatively, its recording in the book is an honor and a judgment concerning them.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p405#2/r14.anchor: أحدهما : أن يكون له فضلا له وحكما به .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p405#2/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p405#2/r15.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p405#2/r15.claim: Alternatively, the record allows the angels to learn the matter at its appointed time.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p405#2/r15.anchor: الثاني : ليعلم به ملائكته في وقته .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p405#2/r16.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p405#2/r16.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p405#2/r16.claim: ‘My Lord does not stray or forget’ may mean He does not err about it or leave it undone.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p405#2/r16.anchor: أحدهما : لا يخطىء فيه ولا يتركه .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p405#2/r17.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p405#2/r17.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p405#2/r17.claim: Ibn Abbas alternatively reads the line as saying the book does not go missing from God and God does not forget what it contains.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p405#2/r17.anchor: الثاني : لا يضل الكتاب عن ربي , ولا ينسى ربي ما في الكتاب , قاله ابن عباس .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p405#2/r18.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p405#2/r18.speaker: مقاتل
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p405#2/r18.claim: Musa did not yet know the earlier generations' history, which he learned from the Torah revealed only after Pharaoh's death and drowning.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p405#2/r18.anchor: قال مقاتل : ولم يكن في ذلك [ الوقت ] عند موسى علم القرون الأولى , لأنه علمها من التوراة , ولم تنزل عليه إلا بعد هلاك فرعون وغرقه .

MUJAHID:v1p397#4/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p397#4/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p397#4/r1.claim: The statements that God does not stray and does not forget express one and the same thing.
MUJAHID:v1p397#4/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد ﴿ لا يضل ربي ولا ينسى ﴾ قال هما شيء واحد

MUQATIL:20:48-53/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:48-53/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:20:48-53/r6.claim: Their knowledge is in the Preserved Tablet; God neither errs in that record nor forgets what it contains.
MUQATIL:20:48-53/r6.anchor: ف { قال علمها عند ربي في كتاب } يعنى اللوح المحفوظ { لا يضل ربي } يعنى لا يخطئ ذلك الكتاب ربى

MUQATIL:20:48-53/r7.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:48-53/r7.speaker: author
MUQATIL:20:48-53/r7.claim: After revealing the Torah, God informed Moses and explained the earlier generations in it.
MUQATIL:20:48-53/r7.anchor: فلما أنزل الله، عز وجل، عليه التوراة أعلمه، وبين له فيها القرون، الأولى.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p57#4/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p57#4/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p57#4/r1.claim: Moses answers that knowledge of past generations is with God, recorded in the Preserved Tablet; this is unseen knowledge reserved to Him, and Moses knows only what God reveals.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p57#4/r1.anchor: هذا سؤال عن الغيب وقد استاثر الله به لا يعلمه إلا هو وما أنا إلا عبد مثلك لا أعلم منه إلا ما أخبرني به

NASAFI-FULL:v3p57#4/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p57#4/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p57#4/r2.claim: Lā yaḍillu means God does not miss or err, including in determining people’s felicity or misery.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p57#4/r2.anchor: أي لا يخطئ في سعادة الناس وشقاوتهم

NASAFI-FULL:v3p57#4/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p57#4/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p57#4/r3.claim: Lā yansā means He does not forget their reward or punishment; alternatively, the record preserves what He knows so the angels can see creatures’ actions accord with His knowledge.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p57#4/r3.anchor: ثوابهم وعقابهم وقيل لا ينسى ما علم فيذكره الكتاب

QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52/r4.claim: Another interpretation identifies the book recording their deeds as a book kept with one of the angels.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52/r4.anchor: وقيل: هو كتاب مع بعض الملائكة.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52/r5.claim: This verse and similar passages support writing down knowledge, since memory can fail through error or forgetting and writing preserves what one may not retain.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52/r5.anchor: هذه الآية ونظائرها مما تقدم ويأتي تدل على تدوين العلوم وكتبها لئلا تنسى.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52/r6.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52/r6.claim: When asked whether his lessons should be written, Qatada replied that God's own statement that He writes gives no reason not to write what one hears.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52/r6.anchor: عن قتادة أنه قيل له: أنكتب ما نسمع منك؟ قال: وما يمنعك أن تكتب وقد أخبرك اللطيف الخبير

QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52/r7.speaker: النبي
QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52/r7.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that after creating creation, God wrote in a book kept with Him that His mercy prevails over His wrath; al-Qurtubi cites Sahih Muslim.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52/r7.anchor: لما قضى الله الخلق كتب في كتاب على نفسه فهو موضوع عنده إن رحمتي تغلب غضبي

QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52/r8.speaker: النبي
QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52/r8.claim: An Ansari who enjoyed the Prophet's hadith but could not remember it asked for help; the Prophet told him to use his right hand and gestured toward writing.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52/r8.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال: كان رجل من الأنصار يجلس إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يستمع منه الحديث ويعجبه ولا يحفظه

QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52/r9.claim: The Prophet ordered that his sermon at the pilgrimage be written for Abu Shah, a Yemeni who requested it; Muslim transmits the report.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52/r9.anchor: بكتب الخطبة التي خطب بها في الحج لأبي شاه رجل من اليمن لما سأله كتبها. أخرجه مسلم.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52#2/r1.speaker: النبي
QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52#2/r1.claim: A report through ʿAmr ibn Shuʿayb, from his father and grandfather, attributes to the Prophet the instruction to bind knowledge by writing.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52#2/r1.anchor: قيدوا العلم بالكتابة " وقال معاوية بن قرة

QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52#2/r2.speaker: معاوية بن قرة
QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52#2/r2.claim: Whoever does not write knowledge has not made his knowledge count as knowledge.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52#2/r2.anchor: وقال معاوية بن قرة: من لم يكتب العلم لم يعد علمه علما.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52#2/r3.speaker: أبو سعيد
QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52#2/r3.claim: Asked whether his hadith should be written, Abu Saʿid objected that this would turn them into a Qurʾan and urged listeners to memorize as the earlier generation had.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52#2/r3.anchor: فروى أبو نضرة قال: قيل لأبي سعيد: أنكتب حديثكم هذا؟ قال: لم تجعلونه قرآنا؟ ولكن احفظوا كما حفظنا.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52#2/r4.speaker: الشعبي، يونس بن عبيد، خالد الحذاء، ابن عون، الزهري
QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52#2/r4.claim: A group disapproved of writing, including al-Shaʿbi, Yunus ibn ʿUbayd, Khalid al-Hadhdha, Ibn ʿAwn, and al-Zuhri.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52#2/r4.anchor: وممن كان لا يكتب الشعبي ويونس بن عبيد وخالد الحذاء قال خالد: ما كتبت شيئا قط إلا حديثا واحدا

QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52#2/r5.speaker: خالد الحذاء
QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52#2/r5.claim: Khalid says he wrote only one hadith, then erased it after memorizing it.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52#2/r5.anchor: قال خالد: ما كتبت شيئا قط إلا حديثا واحدا، فلما حفظته محوته

QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52#2/r6.speaker: محمد بن سيرين، عاصم بن ضمرة
QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52#2/r6.claim: Some wrote hadith and erased the notes after memorizing them; Ibn Sirin and ʿAsim ibn Damra are named.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52#2/r6.anchor: وقد كان بعضهم يكتب فإذا حفظ محاه منهم محمد بن سيرين وعاصم بن ضمرة.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52#2/r7.speaker: هشام بن حسان
QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52#2/r7.claim: Hisham says he once wrote the hadith of al-Aʿmaq, then erased it after memorizing it; the report concerns the Romans descending at al-Aʿmaq or Dabiq before the Hour.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52#2/r7.anchor: ما كتبت حديثا قط إلا حديث الأعماق فلما حفظته محوته. قلت: وقد ذكرنا عن خالد الحذاء مثل هذا.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52#2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52#2/r8.speaker: الأعمش، عبد الله بن إدريس، هشيم
QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52#2/r8.claim: Some scholars, including al-Aʿmash, ʿAbd Allah ibn Idris, and Hushaym, memorized first and then wrote, as a safeguard for memory.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52#2/r8.anchor: وكان بعضهم يحفظ ثم يكتب ما يحفظ منهم الأعمش وعبد الله بن إدريس وهشيم وغيرهم. وهذا احتياط على الحفظ.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52#2/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52#2/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52#2/r9.claim: Al-Qurtubi holds that writing is generally preferable, supported by scripture, reports, and the practice of senior Companions and Successors.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52#2/r9.anchor: والكتب أولى على الجملة، وبه وردت الآي والأحاديث وهو مروي عن عمر وعلي وجابر وأنس رضي الله عنهم

QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52#2/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52#2/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52#2/r10.claim: Writing preserves knowledge and enables comparison, study, review, memorization, discussion, questioning, checking transmitters, and confidence in what they transmit.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52#2/r10.anchor: فإن العلم لا يضبط إلا بالكتاب، ثم بالمقابلة والمدارسة والتعهد والتحفظ والمذاكرة والسؤال والفحص عن الناقلين

QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52#2/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52#2/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52#2/r11.claim: Early scholars avoided writing because chains were close and recent, fearing writers would rely on notes, neglect memorization, or fail to act on knowledge.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52#2/r11.anchor: وإنما كره الكتب من كره من الصدر الأول لقرب العهد، وتقارب الإسناد لئلا يعتمده الكاتب فيهمله

QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52#2/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52#2/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52#2/r12.claim: With time elapsed, longer chains, varied transmission paths, and the risks of forgetting and error, recording knowledge in writing is more beneficial and better supported.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52#2/r12.anchor: فأما والوقت متباعد، والإسناد غير متقارب، والطرق مختلفة، والنقلة متشابهون، وآفة النسيان معترضة

QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52#3/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52#3/r1.speaker: النبي
QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52#3/r1.claim: A report from Abu Saʿid says the Prophet prohibited writing from him and ordered that anything written besides the Qurʾan be erased; al-Qurtubi answers that this was earlier and superseded.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52#3/r1.anchor: لا تكتبوا عني ومن كتب غير القرآن فليمحه " خرجه مسلم فالجواب

QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52#3/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52#3/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52#3/r2.claim: Al-Qurtubi says the prohibition also served to prevent material outside the Qurʾan from being confused with it.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52#3/r2.anchor: وأيضا كان ذلك لئلا يخلط بالقرآن ما ليس منه.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52#3/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52#3/r3.speaker: أبو سعيد
QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52#3/r3.claim: A report says Abu Saʿid and others sought permission to write, but the Prophet refused; al-Qurtubi says, if preserved, it was before the Hijra when writing might distract from the Qurʾan.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52#3/r3.anchor: حرصنا أن يأذن لنا النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في الكتابة فأبى إن كان محفوظا فهو قبل الهجرة

QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52#3/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52#3/r4.speaker: أبو بكر الخطيب
QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52#3/r4.claim: Al-Khatib advises writing hadith in black ink rather than ordinary liquid ink, since black lasts and ink endures through the ages.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52#3/r4.anchor: ينبغي أن يكتب الحديث بالسواد ثم الحبر خاصة دون المداد لأن السواد أصبغ الألوان، والحبر أبقاها على مر الدهور.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52#3/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52#3/r5.speaker: الشافعي
QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52#3/r5.claim: Seeing ink on Ahmad ibn Hanbal's shirt, al-Shafiʿi called it a mark of dignity: black to the eye and white in insight.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52#3/r5.anchor: إن الحبر على الثوب من المروءة لأن صورته في الأبصار سواد، وفي البصائر بياض.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52#3/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52#3/r6.speaker: خالد بن يزيد
QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52#3/r6.claim: Khalid ibn Yazid compares ink on a hadith scholar's clothing to perfume on a bride's clothing.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52#3/r6.anchor: وقال خالد بن يزيد: الحبر في ثوب صاحب الحديث مثل الخلوق في ثوب العروس.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52#3/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52#3/r7.speaker: أبو عبد الله البلوي
QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52#3/r7.claim: His poem compares men's ink to women's saffron perfume and says each adornment suits its wearer's clothing.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52#3/r7.anchor: مداد المحابر طيب الرجال وطيب النساء من الزعفران فهذا يليق بأثواب ذا

QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52#3/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52#3/r8.speaker: الماوردي
QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52#3/r8.claim: Al-Mawardi reports that ʿAbd Allah ibn Sulayman covered a yellow stain with ink, saying ink suited scholars better than saffron.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52#3/r8.anchor: رأى على بعض ثيابه أثر صفرة فأخذ من مداد الدواة وطلاه به ثم قال: المداد بنا أحسن من الزعفران

QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52#3/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52#3/r9.speaker: الشاعر
QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52#3/r9.claim: The accompanying poem says saffron is the fragrance of girls and ink from inkwells the fragrance of men.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52#3/r9.anchor: إنما الزعفران عطر العذارى ومداد الدوي عطر الرجال

QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52#3/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52#3/r10.speaker: الزجاج
QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52#3/r10.claim: One view treats “my Lord does not err or forget” as a new sentence that begins after “in a book”; “err” means perish, as in 32:10.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52#3/r10.anchor: إنه ابتداء كلام، تنزيه لله تعالى عن هاتين الصفتين. وقد كان الكلام تم في قوله: «في كتاب». وكذا قال الزجاج

QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52#3/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52#3/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52#3/r11.claim: “Does not err” means God does not make mistakes in governance; He delays or hastens matters for wisdom.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52#3/r11.anchor: «لا يضل» لا يخطىء قاله ابن عباس أي لا يخطىء في التدبير، فمن أنظره فلحكمة أنظره

QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52#3/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52#3/r12.speaker: ابن الأعرابي
QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52#3/r12.claim: “Does not err” means nothing is absent from God and He is absent from nothing; the root can mean disappearance.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52#3/r12.anchor: قال ابن الأعرابي: أصل الضلال الغيبوبة يقال: ضل الناسي إذا غاب عنه حفظ الشيء.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52#3/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52#3/r13.speaker: الزجاج، النحاس
QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52#3/r13.claim: Their preferred explanation is that God needs no book: no knowledge or recognition of anything escapes Him, and He forgets nothing He knows.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52#3/r13.anchor: قاله الزجاج أيضا وقال النحاس وهو أشبهها بالمعنى

QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52#3/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52#3/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52#3/r14.claim: Al-Qurtubi says this explanation returns to Ibn al-Aʿrabi's view that nothing is absent from God.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52#3/r14.anchor: قلت: وهذا القول راجع إلى معنى قول ابن الأعرابي.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52#3/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52#3/r15.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52#3/r15.claim: A fifth grammatical view makes “does not err or forget” an adjective of “book,” meaning the book is not lost from God and is not forgotten; the sentence therefore continues without a pause after “book.”
QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52#3/r15.anchor: إن { لا يضل ربي ولا ينسى } في موضع الصفة ل«كتاب» أي الكتاب غير ضال عن الله عز وجل

QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52#3/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52#3/r16.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52#3/r16.claim: Arabic usage allows saying that something “was lost from me” when it could not be found, and that one lost it by leaving it somewhere and not finding it.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52#3/r16.anchor: تقول العرب: ضلني الشيء إذا لم أجده، وأضللته أنا إذا تركته في موضع فلم تجده فيه.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52#3/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52#3/r17.speaker: الحسن، قتادة، عيسى بن عمر، ابن محيصن، عاصم الجحدري، ابن كثير عن شبل
QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52#3/r17.claim: These reciters read yudill with ḍamma on the yāʾ, meaning “my Lord does not cause it to be lost and does not forget it.”
QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52#3/r17.anchor: وقرأ الحسن وقتادة وعيسى بن عمر وابن محيصن وعاصم الجحدري وابن كثير فيما روى شبل عنه «لا يضل» بضم الياء

QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52#3/r18.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52#3/r18.speaker: ابن عرفة
QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52#3/r18.claim: Ibn ʿArafa says Arabic ḍalāla is taking a wrong path, while aḍalla means to lose or waste something; this supports the reading “does not let it be lost.”
QURTUBI-FULL:20:51-52#3/r18.anchor: قال ابن عرفة: الضلالة عند العرب سلوك سبيل غير القصد يقال: ضل عن الطريق، وأضل الشيء إذا أضاعه.

RAZI-FULL:v22p58/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p58/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p58/r8.claim: Razi prefers that Pharaoh feared Moses’ proof would expose his falsehood before the people, so he distracted Moses with old stories; Moses declined to discuss them and resumed the proof of divine oneness.
RAZI-FULL:v22p58/r8.anchor: وهو الأظهر أن فرعون لما قال : { فمن ربكما ياموسى * موسى } فذكر موسى عليه السلام دليلا ظاهرا وبرهانا باهرا على هذا المطلوب

RAZI-FULL:v22p58#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p58#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p58#2/r1.claim: One interpretation says God recorded earlier peoples’ affairs in a book so angels could see them, gaining another proof of His knowledge and freedom from heedlessness.
RAZI-FULL:v22p58#2/r1.anchor: معناه أنه سبحانه أثبت تلك الأحكام في كتاب عنده لكون ما كتبه فيه يظهر للملائكة فيكون ذلك زيادة لهم في الاستدلال

RAZI-FULL:v22p58#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p58#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p58#2/r2.claim: Razi objects that speaking of a book may imply, especially to an unbeliever being addressed, that God needs the book in order to know.
RAZI-FULL:v22p58#2/r2.anchor: قوله : { فى كتاب } يوهم احتياجه سبحانه وتعالى في ذلك العلم إلى ذلك الكتاب وهذا وإن كان غير واجب لا محالة ولكنه لا أقل من أنه يوهمه

RAZI-FULL:v22p58#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p58#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p58#2/r3.claim: A second interpretation compares the continued presence of these known matters to writing in a book, emphasizing that none leaves God’s knowledge.
RAZI-FULL:v22p58#2/r3.anchor: أن تفسير ذلك بأن بقاء تلك المعلومات في علمه سبحانه كبقاء المكتوب في الكتاب فيكون الغرض من هذا الكلام تأكيد القول

RAZI-FULL:v22p58#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p58#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p58#2/r4.claim: The following statement that God neither strays nor forgets supports the second interpretation by affirming that His knowledge does not fade.
RAZI-FULL:v22p58#2/r4.anchor: وهذا التفسير مؤكد بقوله بعد ذلك : { لا يضل ربى ولا ينسى }

RAZI-FULL:v22p58#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p58#2/r5.speaker: مجاهد
RAZI-FULL:v22p58#2/r5.claim: Mujahid takes “does not stray” and “does not forget” as synonymous: nothing escapes God or is hidden from Him.
RAZI-FULL:v22p58#2/r5.anchor: فقال بعضهم معنى اللفظين واحد أي لا يذهب عليه شيء ولا يخفى عليه وهذا قول مجاهد

RAZI-FULL:v22p58#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p58#2/r6.speaker: الأكثرون
RAZI-FULL:v22p58#2/r6.claim: Most commentators distinguish between the two expressions and offer several explanations.
RAZI-FULL:v22p58#2/r6.anchor: والأكثرون على الفرق بينهما ، ثم ذكروا وجوها

RAZI-FULL:v22p58#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p58#2/r7.speaker: القفال
RAZI-FULL:v22p58#2/r7.claim: Al-Qaffal’s preferred distinction is that God does not stray from knowing anything and never forgets what He knows; the first affirms universal knowledge and the second its permanence, excluding change.
RAZI-FULL:v22p58#2/r7.anchor: وهو الأحسن ما قاله القفال لا يضل عن الأشياء ومعرفتها وما علم من ذلك لم ينسه

RAZI-FULL:v22p58#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p58#2/r8.speaker: مقاتل
RAZI-FULL:v22p58#2/r8.claim: Muqatil says the Lord does not err in the book or forget what it contains.
RAZI-FULL:v22p58#2/r8.anchor: قال مقاتل : لا يخطىء ذلك الكتاب ربي ولا ينسى ما فيه

RAZI-FULL:v22p58#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p58#2/r9.speaker: الحسن
RAZI-FULL:v22p58#2/r9.claim: Al-Hasan interprets the words as God neither erring about nor forgetting the time of resurrection.
RAZI-FULL:v22p58#2/r9.anchor: قال الحسن لا يخطىء وقت البعث ولا ينساه

RAZI-FULL:v22p58#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p58#2/r10.speaker: أبو عمرو
RAZI-FULL:v22p58#2/r10.claim: Abu ʿAmr explains the root meaning of straying as absence: nothing is absent from God and God is absent from nothing.
RAZI-FULL:v22p58#2/r10.anchor: قال أبو عمرو أصل الضلال الغيبوبة والمعنى لا يغيب عن شيء ولا يغيب عنه شيء

RAZI-FULL:v22p58#2/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p58#2/r11.speaker: ابن جرير
RAZI-FULL:v22p58#2/r11.claim: Ibn Jarir says God does not err in managing affairs by judging a wrong thing correct, and does not forget what He knows.
RAZI-FULL:v22p58#2/r11.anchor: قال ابن جرير لا يخطىء في التدبير فيعتقد في غير الصواب كونه صوابا وإذا عرفه لا ينساه

RAZI-FULL:v22p58#2/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p58#2/r12.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p58#2/r12.claim: Razi considers the proposed meanings close and identifies Al-Qaffal’s first distinction as the correct interpretation.
RAZI-FULL:v22p58#2/r12.anchor: وهذه الوجوه متقاربة والتحقيق هو الأول

STUDYQURAN:20:51/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:51/r2.speaker: Aj
STUDYQURAN:20:51/r2.claim: Moses' answer says this is an unfathomable matter known only to God.
STUDYQURAN:20:51/r2.anchor: Moses’ reply confirms that knowledge of this matter is an unfathomable affair that none knows but God

STUDYQURAN:20:51/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:51/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:20:51/r3.claim: The Book in which this knowledge is recorded is the Preserved Tablet.
STUDYQURAN:20:51/r3.anchor: By a Book is meant the Preserved Tablet

SAMIN-DURR:20:52/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:52/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:52/r1.claim: The first analysis makes عند ربي the predicate; في كتاب may depend on its existential governor, modify the hidden subject circumstantially, or be a second predicate.
SAMIN-DURR:20:52/r1.anchor: قوله: { قال علمها عند ربي } في خبر هذا المبتدأ أوجه، أحدها: أنه " عند ربي " وعلى هذا فقوله " في كتاب " متعلق بما تعلق به الظرف من الاستقرار

SAMIN-DURR:20:52/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:52/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:52/r2.claim: The second analysis makes في كتاب the predicate; عند ربي may depend on its existential governor or be a circumstantial phrase, whose precedence before a semantic governor is disputed.
SAMIN-DURR:20:52/r2.anchor: الثاني: أن الخبر قوله " في كتاب " فعلى هذا قوله " عند ربي " معمول للاستقرار الذي تعلق به " في كتاب "

SAMIN-DURR:20:52/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:52/r3.speaker: الأخفش
SAMIN-DURR:20:52/r3.claim: He allows a circumstantial phrase before its semantic governor and adduces 39:67 and a line of poetry as evidence.
SAMIN-DURR:20:52/r3.anchor: والأخفش يجيزه ويستدل بقراءة { والسماوات مطويات بيمينه } [الزمر: 67] وقوله:

SAMIN-DURR:20:52/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:52/r4.speaker: بعض النحويين
SAMIN-DURR:20:52/r4.claim: They say an adverbial circumstantial phrase is readily fronted when its governor is semantic.
SAMIN-DURR:20:52/r4.anchor: وقال بعض النحويين: إنه إذا كان العامل معنويا، والحال ظرف أو عديله، حسن التقديم عند الأخفش وغيره، وهذا منه.

SAMIN-DURR:20:52/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:52/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:52/r5.claim: With في كتاب as predicate, عند ربي may also modify the knowledge itself or be circumstantial to the genitive pronoun.
SAMIN-DURR:20:52/r5.anchor: أو يكون ظرفا للعلم نفسه، أو يكون حالا من المضاف إليه وهو الضمير في " عليها ".

SAMIN-DURR:20:52/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:52/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:52/r6.claim: If عند ربي is already the predicate, في كتاب cannot modify علمها, since an unrelated phrase would split a verbal noun from its complement and a relative must complete its clause first.
SAMIN-DURR:20:52/r6.anchor: ولا يجوز أن يكون " في كتاب " متعلقا ب " علمها " على قولنا إن " عند ربي " الخبر كما جاز تعلق " عند " به

SAMIN-DURR:20:52/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:52/r7.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:20:52/r7.claim: A third analysis treats both prepositional phrases as a single semantic predicate, like “sweet and sour.”
SAMIN-DURR:20:52/r7.anchor: الثالث: أن يكون الظرف وحرف الجر معا خبرا واحدا في المعنى، فيكون بمنزلة " هذا حلو حامض " قاله أبو البقاء

SAMIN-DURR:20:52/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:52/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:52/r8.claim: He objects that each phrase independently supplies predicative meaning, unlike حلو حامض.
SAMIN-DURR:20:52/r8.anchor: وفيه نظر؛ إذ كل منها يستقل بفائدة الخبرية، بخلاف " هذا حلو حامض ".

SAMIN-DURR:20:52/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:52/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:52/r9.claim: The pronoun in علمها most clearly refers to the past generations; a second view takes it as the Resurrection, implied by the question about nations' return.
SAMIN-DURR:20:52/r9.anchor: والضمير في " علمها " فيه وجهان، أظهرهما: عوده على القرون. والثاني: عوده على القيامة

SAMIN-DURR:20:52#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:52#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:52#2/r1.claim: لا يضل ربي may modify كتاب as a genitive adjective with an omitted object: a book that my Lord does not let go astray or fail to preserve.
SAMIN-DURR:20:52#2/r1.anchor: قوله: { لا يضل ربي } في هذه الجملة وجهان، أحدهما: أنها في محل جر صفة ل " كتاب " ، والعائد محذوف، تقديره: في كتاب لا يضله ربي، أو لا يضل حفظه ربي

SAMIN-DURR:20:52#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:52#2/r2.speaker: قيل
SAMIN-DURR:20:52#2/r2.claim: A second estimate makes كتاب the subject of يضل and ربي an honorific accusative: the book cannot lead my Lord astray.
SAMIN-DURR:20:52#2/r2.anchor: وقيل: تقديره: الكتاب ربي. فيكون في " يضل " ضمير يعود على " كتاب " ، وربي منصوب على التعظيم.

SAMIN-DURR:20:52#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:52#2/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:52#2/r3.claim: On this analysis, عن ربي is understood before the phrase and omitted for expansive usage; ضللت and ضللته are known forms, with fatḥa more common.
SAMIN-DURR:20:52#2/r3.anchor: وكان الأصل: عن ربي، فحذف الحرف اتساعا، يقال: ضللت كذا وضللته بفتح اللام وكسرها، لغتان مشهورتان وشهراهما الفتح.

SAMIN-DURR:20:52#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:52#2/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:52#2/r4.claim: Alternatively, لا يضل ربي is an independent sentence spoken to report God's knowledge.
SAMIN-DURR:20:52#2/r4.anchor: الثاني: أنها مستأنفة لا محل لها من الإعراب ساقها تبارك وتعالى لمجرد الإخبار بذلك حكاية عن موسى.

SAMIN-DURR:20:52#2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:52#2/r5.speaker: الحسن وقتادة والجحدري وعيسى الثقفي وابن محيصن وحماد بن سلمة
SAMIN-DURR:20:52#2/r5.claim: They read لا يضل with ḍamma on yāʾ, meaning my Lord does not cause the book to be lost; ربي is the subject.
SAMIN-DURR:20:52#2/r5.anchor: وقرأ الحسن وقتادة والجحدري وعيسى الثقفي وابن محيصن وحماد بن سلمة " لا يضل " بضم الياء أي: لا يضل ربي الكتاب

SAMIN-DURR:20:52#2/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:52#2/r6.speaker: قيل
SAMIN-DURR:20:52#2/r6.claim: An alternative for the ḍamma reading says no one can lead my Lord away from knowledge of the book, with رب منصوب honorifically.
SAMIN-DURR:20:52#2/r6.anchor: وقيل: تقديره: لا يضل أحد ربي عن علمه أي: عن علم الكتاب، فيكون الرب منصوبا على التعظيم.

SAMIN-DURR:20:52#2/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:52#2/r7.speaker: الرماني
SAMIN-DURR:20:52#2/r7.claim: He distinguishes ضللت منزلي for losing one's way from أضللت بعيري for losing one's animal.
SAMIN-DURR:20:52#2/r7.anchor: وفرق بعضهم بين ضللت وأضللت فقال: " ضللت منزلي " ، بغير ألف، و " أضللت بعيري " ونحوه من الحيوان بالألف. نقل ذلك الرماني عن العرب

SAMIN-DURR:20:52#2/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:52#2/r8.speaker: الفراء
SAMIN-DURR:20:52#2/r8.claim: He says ضللت may mean misplacing or failing to find something, while أضللت is used when an animal escapes and is lost.
SAMIN-DURR:20:52#2/r8.anchor: وقال الفراء: " يقال: ضللت الشيء إذا أخطأت في مكانه وضللت لغتان، فلم تهتد له

SAMIN-DURR:20:52#3/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:52#3/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:52#3/r1.claim: The subject of ينسى may be ربي, who does not forget what He recorded in the book.
SAMIN-DURR:20:52#3/r1.anchor: أحدهما: أنه عائد على " ربي " أي: ولا ينسى ربي ما أثبته في الكتاب.

SAMIN-DURR:20:52#3/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:52#3/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:52#3/r2.claim: Alternatively, the subject is كتاب by metaphor, as in 18:49 where the record is said to enumerate.
SAMIN-DURR:20:52#3/r2.anchor: والثاني: أن الفاعل ضمير عائد على الكتاب على سبيل المجاز، كما أسند إليه الإحصاء مجازا في قوله

TAB-FULL:v16p82/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p82/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p82/r1.claim: Pharaoh asks why earlier nations failed to believe and worship God alone if all beings were created and sustained by the Lord Moses describes.
TAB-FULL:v16p82/r1.anchor: لم تقر بما تقول، ولم تصدق بما تدعو إليه، ولم تخلص له العبادة

TAB-FULL:v16p82/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p82/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p82/r2.claim: Moses answers that their knowledge is with God in the Preserved Record; he does not know why some went astray from God's religion.
TAB-FULL:v16p82/r2.anchor: علم هذه الأمم التي مضت من قبلنا فيما فعلت من ذلك، عند ربي في كتاب: يعني في أم الكتاب، لا علم لي بأمرها

TAB-FULL:v16p82/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p82/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p82/r3.claim: God does not err in His governance: whether He punished those nations in life or deferred punishment until Judgment, His act is right and wise.
TAB-FULL:v16p82/r3.anchor: لا يخطئ ربي في تدبيره وأفعاله، فإن كان عذب تلك القرون في عاجل، وعجل هلاكها، فالصواب ما فعل

TAB-FULL:v16p82/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p82/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p82/r4.claim: God does not forget by leaving undone an act that is wise and right.
TAB-FULL:v16p82/r4.anchor: فيترك فعل ما فعله حكمة وصواب

TAB-FULL:v16p82/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p82/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v16p82/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses the two clauses as God neither erring nor forgetting.
TAB-FULL:v16p82/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {في كتاب لا يضل ربي ولا ينسى} [طه: 52] يقول: لا يخطئ ربي ولا ينسى

TAB-FULL:v16p82/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p82/r7.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v16p82/r7.claim: Mujahid says “does not err” and “does not forget” express one meaning.
TAB-FULL:v16p82/r7.anchor: عن مجاهد، قوله: {لا يضل ربي ولا ينسى} [طه: 52] قال: هما شيء واحد

TAB-FULL:v16p82/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p82/r8.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p82/r8.claim: In Arabic, missing a fixed place is expressed with ḍalla, while losing a moving animal that wanders off is expressed with aḍalla.
TAB-FULL:v16p82/r8.anchor: ضل فلان منزله: إذا أخطأه، يضله بغير ألف، وكذلك ذلك في كل ما كان من شيء ثابت لا يبرح

TABATABAI:20:49-79#3/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:49-79#3/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:49-79#3/r2.claim: Moses answers that God knows the bygone generations in full detail: none of their persons or deeds escapes him or disappears from him.
TABATABAI:20:49-79#3/r2.anchor: فأطلق العلم بها فلا يفوته شيء من أشخاصهم وأعمالهم وجعلها عند الله فلا تغيب عنه ولا تفوته

TABATABAI:20:49-79#3/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:49-79#3/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:49-79#3/r3.claim: The record in a book confirms that this knowledge is preserved and unchanging; the indefinite 'book' conveys immense scope and precision.
TABATABAI:20:49-79#3/r3.anchor: ليؤكد به أنه مثبت محفوظ من غير أن يتغير عن حاله وقد نكر الكتاب ليدل به على فخامة أمره

TABATABAI:20:49-79#3/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:49-79#3/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:49-79#3/r4.claim: The past generations' recompense is problematic only if they are unknown, but they remain known and recorded without error, alteration, or disappearance.
TABATABAI:20:49-79#3/r4.anchor: إنما يشكل لو جهل ولم يعلم بها لكنها معلومة لربي محفوظة عنده في كتاب لا يتطرق إليه خطأ ولا تغيير ولا غيبة

TABATABAI:20:49-79#3/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:49-79#3/r5.speaker: بعضهم
TABATABAI:20:49-79#3/r5.claim: Some interpreters take the negation to cover both initial ignorance and ignorance arising after knowledge.
TABATABAI:20:49-79#3/r5.anchor: نفي للجهل الإبتدائي والجهل بعد العلم على ما نقل عن بعضهم

TABATABAI:20:49-79#3/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:49-79#3/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:49-79#3/r6.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī prefers that both verbs deny ignorance after knowledge: error misplaces what is known, while forgetting is its loss after being known.
TABATABAI:20:49-79#3/r6.anchor: ولكن الظاهر أن الجملة مسوقة لنفي الجهل بعد العلم بقسميه

TABATABAI:20:49-79#3/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:49-79#3/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:49-79#3/r7.claim: Together, the clauses establish that God knows the earlier generations and cannot later become ignorant of them, so he can requite them.
TABATABAI:20:49-79#3/r7.anchor: فيفيد مجموع الآية أنه عالم بالقرون الأولى ولا سبيل إليه للجهل بعد العلم فيجازيهم على ما علم

TABATABAI:20:49-79#3/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:49-79#3/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:49-79#3/r8.claim: The final clause completes the explanation by answering the imagined objection that vanished people and erased traces can no longer be distinguished: no deed is confused or forgotten by God.
TABATABAI:20:49-79#3/r8.anchor: كأنه دفع دخل مقدر كأنما قيل إنها وإن علم بها يوما فهي اليوم باطلة الذوات معفوة الآثار

TABATABAI:20:49-79#3/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:49-79#3/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:49-79#3/r9.claim: The clause is set off without a conjunction because it supplies this answer to the anticipated objection.
TABATABAI:20:49-79#3/r9.anchor: ولذا أوردت الجملة مفصولة غير معطوفة

TABATABAI:20:49-79#3/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:49-79#3/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:49-79#3/r10.claim: Calling God 'Lord' grounds the argument: absolute ownership and governance of all things cannot coexist with ignorance of anything under his care.
TABATABAI:20:49-79#3/r10.anchor: أن فرض الربوبية لا يجامع فرض الجهل بالمربوب

TABATABAI:20:49-79#3/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:49-79#3/r11.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:49-79#3/r11.claim: If anything owned and governed by God were unknown to him, it would be both present through him and absent from him, a contradiction.
TABATABAI:20:49-79#3/r11.anchor: لا حاجب بينهما ولا فاصل وهو الحضور الذي نسميه علما وقد فرضناه مجهولا أي غائبا عنه هذا خلف

TABATABAI:20:49-79#4/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:49-79#4/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:49-79#4/r1.claim: Moses says 'my Lord' because the question concerns the bygone generations he is describing; saying 'our Lord' would not express that relation as directly.

TABATABAI:20:49-79#4/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:49-79#4/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:49-79#4/r2.claim: The second 'my Lord' parallels the first, though al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī questions whether either is an instance of replacing a pronoun with an explicit noun because the clauses are separated.
TABATABAI:20:49-79#4/r2.anchor: والنكتة في { ربى } الثاني هي نظيره ما في { ربى } الأول

TABATABAI:20:49-79#4/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:49-79#4/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:49-79#4/r4.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī calls this diversion-and-history explanation one of the strangest interpretations, contrasting it with the questions' connection to the preceding argument.
TABATABAI:20:49-79#4/r4.anchor: ومن أعجبها قول كثير منهم أن قول فرعون لموسى

ZAJJAJ:v3p358#2/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p358#2/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p358#2/r5.claim: ‘My Lord does not err or forget’ can mean God does not lose track of the generations or forget them, or that He does not misplace or forget the record.
ZAJJAJ:v3p358#2/r5.anchor: معناه لا يضلها ولا ينساها، ولا يضله ربي ولا ينساه، يعنى به الكتاب.

ZAJJAJ:v3p358#2/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p358#2/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p358#2/r6.claim: Ḍalla has two vowelings; aḍlaltuhu means putting something where its location is unknown, hence causing it to be lost.
ZAJJAJ:v3p358#2/r6.anchor: ومعنى ضللت الشيء وضللت بكسر اللام وفتحها أضله وأضله،

ZAJJAJ:v3p358#2/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p358#2/r7.speaker: أبو إسحاق
ZAJJAJ:v3p358#2/r7.claim: Abū Isḥāq says the reading with fatḥa on the yāʾ means ‘He does not stray from my Lord.’
ZAJJAJ:v3p358#2/r7.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق من قرأ بالفتح فمعناه لا يضل

ZAJJAJ:v3p358#2/r8.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p358#2/r8.speaker: أبو إسحاق
ZAJJAJ:v3p358#2/r8.claim: With ḍamma on the yāʾ, Abū Isḥāq explains that God is not found straying from the record.
ZAJJAJ:v3p358#2/r8.anchor: وإذا ضممت الياء فمعناه لا يوجد ربي ضالا عنها.

TABRISI:20:52-53/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:52-53/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:52-53/r11.claim: The phrase about their knowledge can be parsed with ʿilmuhā as subject and fī kitāb as predicate, while ʿinda rabbī modifies the predicate; it also permits several alternative attachment and predicate analyses.
TABRISI:20:52-53/r11.anchor: علمها مبتدأ وفي كتاب خبره وعند ربي معمول الخبر

TABRISI:20:52-53/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:52-53/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:52-53/r12.claim: In lā yaḍillu rabbī, the prepositional object ʿanhu is omitted, as fīhi is omitted in the verse about a day when no soul avails another.
TABRISI:20:52-53/r12.anchor: لا يضل ربي عنه فحذف الجار والمجرور

TABRISI:20:52-53#2/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:52-53#2/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:52-53#2/r12.claim: Moses says their deeds are preserved with God, who will recompense them; the book is the Preserved Tablet.
TABRISI:20:52-53#2/r12.anchor: أي أعمالهم محفوظة عند الله يجازيهم بها والتقدير علم أعمالهم

TABRISI:20:52-53#2/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:52-53#2/r13.speaker: قيل
