TABRISI:20:52-53#2/r13.claim: Another view says their deeds are written down by the angels.

TABRISI:20:52-53#2/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:52-53#2/r14.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:20:52-53#2/r14.claim: An alternative context is that Pharaoh asked about the generations after Moses called him to believe in resurrection: why had they not been raised?
TABRISI:20:52-53#2/r14.anchor: حين دعاه موسى إلى الإقرار بالبعث أي فما بالهم لم يبعثوا

TABRISI:20:52-53#2/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:52-53#2/r15.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:52-53#2/r15.claim: Lā yaḍillu means nothing escapes God; it may also mean that God does not err.

TABRISI:20:52-53#2/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:52-53#2/r16.speaker: أبو مسلم
TABRISI:20:52-53#2/r16.claim: Abū Muslim says God does not forget what happened to the earlier nations but recompenses them for their deeds.
TABRISI:20:52-53#2/r16.anchor: عن أبي مسلم أي لا ينسى ما كان من أمرهم بل يجازيهم بأعمالهم

TABRISI:20:52-53#2/r17.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:52-53#2/r17.speaker: السدي
TABRISI:20:52-53#2/r17.claim: Al-Suddī explains the phrase as God not neglecting or leaving anything.

THALABI:v6p247/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p247/r8.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p247/r8.claim: Moses says the earlier generations' record is with God in the Preserved Tablet; he refers their knowledge to God because he did not know it, and the Torah was revealed only after Pharaoh's people perished.
THALABI:v6p247/r8.anchor: يعني اللوح المحفوظ، وإنما رد موسى علم ذلك إلى الله سبحانه لأنه لم يعلم ذلك، وإنما نزلت التوراة عليه بعد هلاك فرعون وقومه

THALABI:v6p247/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p247/r9.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p247/r9.claim: The statement that God neither strays nor forgets means He neither errs nor needs to remember.
THALABI:v6p247/r9.anchor: لا يضل ربي أي لا يخطئ ولا ينسى فيتذكر

THALABI:v6p247/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p247/r10.speaker: مجاهد
THALABI:v6p247/r10.claim: Mujahid says the two descriptions of God's knowledge mean the same thing.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p417/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p417/r1.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p417/r1.claim: Abu Ishaq says the generations’ deeds are preserved with God, who will repay them for them.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p417/r1.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق: (أي أعمالهم محفوظة عند الله يجازي بها)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p417/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p417/r2.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p417/r2.claim: Al-Kalbi identifies the book as the Preserved Tablet.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p417/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p417/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p417/r3.claim: Their deeds are written down, so they receive the recompense for what they did, just as Moses’ hearers will be judged for their own deeds; the verse links this to 2:134.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p417/r3.anchor: أعمالهم مكتوبة مثبتة. ومعنى هذا الجواب أنهم يجازون بما عملوا، وأنت تجازى بما تعمل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p417/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p417/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p417/r4.claim: ‘My Lord neither errs nor forgets’ confirms certain recompense: He does not leave an unbeliever unpunished or forget a monotheist’s reward.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p417/r4.anchor: تأكيد وتحقيق للجزاء بالأعمال. قال: يريد لا يترك من كفر به حتى ينتقم منه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p417/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p417/r5.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p417/r5.claim: Al-Kalbi says God does not err or forget any of their affairs, but gives good for good and evil for evil.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p417/r5.anchor: وقال الكلبي: (لا يخطئ ربي ولا ينسى ما كان من أمرهم، حتى يوافيهم بأعمالهم بالحسن حسنا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p417/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p417/r6.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p417/r6.claim: Al-Farra distinguishes losing a movable thing, such as an escaped animal, from missing the location of a fixed thing; the latter is called ḍalaltuhu, not aḍlaltuhu.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p417/r6.anchor: قال الفراء: (يقال أضللت الشيء: إذا ضاع منك مثل: الدابة وما أشبهها إذا انفلت منك

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p417/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p417/r7.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p417/r7.claim: Abu Ishaq says ḍalaltu a thing is to put it somewhere and not know where it is, while aḍlaltuhu is to lose it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p417/r7.anchor: وقال أبو إسحاق: (ضللت الشيء أضله إذا جعلته في مكان لم تدر أين هو، وأضللته أضعته)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p417/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p417/r8.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p417/r8.claim: Abu Ishaq allows the pronoun to refer either to the book—God does not let it go astray or forget it—or to the generations, which He does not lose or forget.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p417/r8.anchor: لا يضله ربي ولا ينساه، يعني به الكتاب، ويجوز لا يضلها ولا ينساها، يعني به القرون

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p417/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p417/r9.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p417/r9.claim: The author takes al-Farra’s sense to mean that God does not make an error.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p417/r9.anchor: والمعنى على ما ذكر الفراء: لا يخطئ ربي كما ذكره الكلبي

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p417/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p417/r10.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p417/r10.claim: On Abu Ishaq’s lexical analysis, ‘does not err’ means ‘does not forget’; Mujahid likewise treats the two clauses as equivalent.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p417/r10.anchor: وعلى ما ذكر أبو إسحاق معنى يضل: ينسى. وقد قال مجاهد: (يضل ربي ولا ينسى هما شيء واحد)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p417/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p417/r11.speaker: السدي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p417/r11.claim: Al-Suddi glosses the phrase as God neither overlooking nor leaving anything.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p417/r11.anchor: وقال السدي: (لا يغفل ولا يترك شيئا)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p417/r12.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p417/r12.speaker: أبو عمرو
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p417/r12.claim: Abu Amr distinguishes a tethered camel that cannot find its place from a loose camel that wanders away, and distinguishes the agent who loses something from the object that goes missing; he derives loss from disappearance.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p417/r12.anchor: وقال أبو عمرو: (يقال أضللت بعيري: إذا كان معقولا فلم يهتد لمكانه، وأضللته إضلالا: إذا كان مطلقا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p418/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p418/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p418/r1.claim: The phrase means that God is absent from nothing and nothing is absent from Him.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p418/r1.anchor: أي: لا يغيب عن شيء ولا يغيب عنه شيء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p418/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p418/r2.speaker: ابن الأنباري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p418/r2.claim: Reporting Muqatil, Ibn al-Anbari says Pharaoh had heard the believer’s warning about earlier nations and wanted to know their histories; Moses then lacked that knowledge because he learned their stories from the Torah, which came only after Pharaoh drowned.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p418/r2.anchor: وقال ابن الأنباري: (مذهب مقاتل في هذه الآية: أن عدو الله فرعون كان قد قال له مؤمن آل فرعون

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p418/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p418/r3.speaker: ابن الأنباري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p418/r3.claim: Ibn al-Anbari rejects the earlier gloss that God does not let the book go astray from Him, arguing that Arabic does not permit dropping the preposition here, as in saying ‘the dirham fell your sleeve’ for ‘from your sleeve.’
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p418/r3.anchor: وذهب الأولون إلى أن المعنى في: {لا يضل ربي} لا يضل الكتاب من ربي. قال وهذا باطل

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:51-54/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:51-54/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:51-54/r2.claim: The book containing their deeds is the Preserved Tablet.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:51-54/r2.anchor: علمها عند ربي في كتاب } وهو اللوح المحفوظ

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:51-54/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:51-54/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:51-54/r3.claim: God does not err or leave an unbeliever without retribution, and does not forget a monotheist before rewarding that person.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:51-54/r3.anchor: لا يخطىء، ومعناه: لا يترك من كفر به حتى ينتقم منه { ولا ينسى } من وحده حتى يجازيه

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p262/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p262/r2.speaker: الحسن
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p262/r2.claim: Al-Hasan explains that God does not lose or forget what is recorded in the book.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p262/r2.anchor: {قال علمها عند ربي في كتاب لا يضل ربي ولا ينسى} [طه: 52] لا يضله فيذهب ولا ينسى ما فيه. هذا تفسير الحسن.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p262/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p262/r4.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p262/r4.claim: Qatada identifies the book as the record of their deeds and lifespans, which God neither loses nor forgets.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p262/r4.anchor: قال قتادة: يعني ذلك الكتاب، {ولا ينسى} [طه: 52] علم أعمالها وآجالها.

IBNMUJAHID:v1p45/r1.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p45/r1.speaker: author
IBNMUJAHID:v1p45/r1.claim: Variation in recitation, like disagreement in legal rulings, is transmitted from Companions and Successors as breadth and mercy for Muslims; many differences are close.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p45/r1.anchor: اختلف الناس في القراءة كما اختلفوا في الأحكام ورويت الآثار بالاختلاف عن الصحابة والتابعين توسعة ورحمة للمسلمين وبعض ذلك قريب من بعض

IBNMUJAHID:v1p45/r2.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p45/r2.speaker: author
IBNMUJAHID:v1p45/r2.claim: Qurʾān transmitters differ in rank, and Ibn Mujāhid intends to describe their ranks, the leading imams, and regional readings and agreements.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p45/r2.anchor: وحملة القرآن متفاضلون في حمله ولنقلة الحروف منازل في نقل حروفه وأنا ذاكر منازلهم ودال على الأئمة منهم

IBNMUJAHID:v1p45/r3.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p45/r3.speaker: author
IBNMUJAHID:v1p45/r3.claim: The qualified imam knows grammar, readings, languages, meanings, defects in readings, and how to assess transmissions; Qurʾān preservers in each region rely on him.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p45/r3.anchor: فمن حملة القرآن المعرب العالم بوجوه الإعراب والقراءات العارف باللغات ومعاني الكلمات البصير بعيب القراءات المنتقد للآثار فذلك الإمام

IBNMUJAHID:v1p45/r4.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p45/r4.speaker: author
IBNMUJAHID:v1p45/r4.claim: A person who can parse correctly but lacks other knowledge reads only in his native idiom, like a Bedouin who cannot change his tongue.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p45/r4.anchor: ومنهم من يعرب ولا يلحن ولا علم له بغير ذلك فذلك كالأعرابي الذي يقرأ بلغته ولا يقدر على تحويل لسانه

IBNMUJAHID:v1p45/r5.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p45/r5.speaker: author
IBNMUJAHID:v1p45/r5.claim: A performer who knows only what he heard, without grammar or other expertise, may forget and lose the parsing distinctions because similar forms and vowel changes recur.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p45/r5.anchor: ومنهم من يؤدي ما سمعه ممن أخذ عنه ليس عنده إلا الأداء لما تعلم لا يعرف الإعراب

IBNMUJAHID:v1p45/r6.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p45/r6.speaker: author
IBNMUJAHID:v1p45/r6.claim: A forgetful memorizer may confuse letters, make an unfamiliar error, attribute it to another, and spread a mistaken reading while appearing credible.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p45/r6.anchor: وقد ينسى الحافظ فيضيع السماع وتشتبه عليه الحروف فيقرأ بلحن لا يعرفه وتدعوه الشبهة إلى أن يرويه عن غيره

IBNMUJAHID:v1p45/r7.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p45/r7.speaker: author
IBNMUJAHID:v1p45/r7.claim: A reading learned from someone who forgot and lost grammatical control should not be followed or treated as proof.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p45/r7.anchor: أو يكون قد قرأ على من نسى وضيع الإعراب ودخلته الشبهة فتوهم فذلك لا يقلد القراءة ولا يحتج بنقله

IBNMUJAHID:v1p45/r8.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p45/r8.speaker: author
IBNMUJAHID:v1p45/r8.claim: A grammarian who knows language and meanings but not transmitted readings may invent an Arabic-possible reading unattested by earlier readers, making it an innovation.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p45/r8.anchor: ومنهم من يعرب قراءته ويبصر المعاني ويعرف اللغات ولا علم له بالقراءات واختلاف الناس والآثار

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p401/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p401/r1.speaker: عمر
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p401/r1.claim: Umar tells people to consult their diwan, explaining that pre-Islamic poetry contains the explanation of the Qur'an and the meanings of Arabic speech.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p401/r1.anchor: فقال عمر رضي الله عنه: يا أيها الناس، عليكم بديوانكم لا يضل، قالوا: وما ديواننا؟ قال: شعر الجاهلية

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p401/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p401/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p401/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas advises readers who cannot understand Qur'anic wording to seek its explanation in poetry, and he himself would cite poetry when asked about Qur'anic Arabic.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p401/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس، أنه كان يسأل عن الشيء من عربية القرآن فينشد الشعر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p401/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p401/r3.speaker: الشافعي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p401/r3.claim: Al-Shafi'i calls Arabic scholars the jinn among humankind.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p401/r3.anchor: سمعت الشافعي رضي الله عنه يقول: أصحاب العربية جن الإنس

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p401/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p401/r4.speaker: عبد الملك بن مروان
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p401/r4.claim: Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan urges people to learn Arabic, calling it visible refinement.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p401/r4.anchor: قال عبد الملك بن مروان (¬5): تعلموا العربية فإنها المروءة الظاهرة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p401/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p401/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p401/r5.claim: Few advance in any discipline without literature, Arabic metrics, and grammar; innovations and misleading desires arise from ignorance of Arabic.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p401/r5.anchor: وقل من تقدم في علم من العلوم إلا بمعرفة الأدب، ومقاييس العربية، والنحو، وما حدثت البدع والأهواء المضلة إلا من الجهل بلغة العرب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p401/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p401/r6.speaker: الشافعي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p401/r6.claim: Al-Shafi'i says that most who became heretics in Iraq did so from ignorance of Arabic and its dialects.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p401/r6.anchor: سمعت الشافعي يقول: عامة من تزندق (¬7) بالعراق لجهلهم بالعربية # ولغات العرب (¬1)

BURHAN:v3p333/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p333/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p333/r1.claim: When a reasonable person faces a bigoted, ignorant opponent, a shift to unrelated speech can loosen resistance; a premise for the original issue is then inserted while attention is elsewhere.
BURHAN:v3p333/r1.anchor: إنه يقرب من الالتفات نقل الكلام إلى غيره وإنما يفعل ذلك إذا ابتلي العاقل بخصم جاهل متعصب فيجب أن يقطع الكلام معه في تلك المسألة

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p6/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p6/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p6/r1.claim: Someone who sees only outward features misses true beauty; an ornamental device should never obscure the meaning it is meant to express.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p6/r1.anchor: إذا لم تشاهد غير حسن شياتها وأعضائها فالحسن عنك مغيب

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p6/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p6/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p6/r2.claim: Overloading speech with decorative devices can obscure or damage meaning, like weighing a bride down with jewelry; skilled writers ornament only after meaning is secure.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p6/r2.anchor: كمن ثقل العروس بأصناف الحلى حتى ينالها من ذلك مكروه في نفسها

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p6/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p6/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p6/r3.claim: Al-Jāḥiẓ’s opening of the Book of Animals prioritizes semantic fit over matching rhyme: he avoids forced pairings such as doubt with perplexity or disagreement with fairness.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p6/r3.anchor: فقد ترك أولا أن يوفق بين الشبهة والحيرة في الإعراب ولم ير أن يقرن الخلاف إلى الإنصاف

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p6/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p6/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p6/r4.claim: Acceptable pun and assonance must be summoned by the meaning; the finest examples arise without contrivance or are sought only because they fit so well, as in al-Shāfiʿī’s answer about nabīdh.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p6/r4.anchor: لا تجد تجنيسا مقبولا ولا سجعا حسنا حتى يكون المعنى هو الذى طلبه واستدعاه وساق نحوه

BURHAN:v2p324/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p324/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p324/r2.claim: Calling properly addresses someone distant, while confidential speech addresses someone near; the account of Moses uses both to convey nearness.
BURHAN:v2p324/r2.anchor: والنداء مخاطبة الابعد والمناجاه مخاطبة الاقرب ولاجل هذه اللطيفة اخبر سبحانه

ITQAN:v2p320/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p320/r7.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p320/r7.claim: “He does not err” means “He does not make a mistake.”
